2027-02-23.title: Tuesday of the Second Week of Lent
readings: Learn to do good. Though your sins are like scarlet, they shall be like snow
To the upright I will show the saving power of God
They do not practise what they teach. The greatest among you will be your servant
2027-02-23.alt: Lenten weekday. The Alleluia is omitted throughout Lent; the Gloria is omitted except on solemnities and feasts. Liturgical colour: violet. Commemoration of St Polycarp, bishop and martyr (its collect may be used).
2027-02-23.verse: The greatest among you will be your servant. All who exalt themselves will be humbled, and all who humble themselves will be exalted.
theo: Isaiah speaks to the rulers of Jerusalem as if they were the rulers of Sodom. Their temple is full of sacrifices, but their hands are full of blood. God does not want more ritual; he wants a changed life: “Wash yourselves; make yourselves clean; remove the evil of your doings from before my eyes; cease to do evil, learn to do good; seek justice, rescue the oppressed, defend the orphan, plead for the widow.” Then comes one of the most tender invitations in the Bible: “Come now, let us argue it out, says the LORD: though your sins are like scarlet, they shall be like snow.” God reasons with his people like a father with a son who has gone wrong. The Psalm says the same: God does not need our bulls and goats; what honours him is a thankful heart and a straight road: “to those who go the right way I will show the salvation of God.”

In the Gospel Jesus warns against a religion of display. The scribes and Pharisees “sit on Moses' seat”, and what they teach from the law should be done, “but do not do as they do, for they do not practice what they teach.” They tie heavy burdens on others and will not lift a finger; they love the best seats and the greetings in the market and the title “rabbi”. Jesus turns this upside down: you have one teacher, one Father, one instructor, the Messiah, and you are all brothers and sisters. “The greatest among you will be your servant.” Lent is a time to check whether our faith is lived or only displayed. Today we remember St Polycarp, bishop of Smyrna, a disciple of St John the Apostle, who served his people for decades and was burned at the stake about the year 155, at the age of eighty-six. When the proconsul told him to curse Christ, he answered (in substance): for eighty-six years I have served him, and he has done me no wrong; how can I blaspheme my King who saved me? He practised what he taught, to the end.
outline: Ask: whom do you trust more, someone who talks well or someone who lives well?
God's invitation to reason and be washed.
Jesus warns against a religion of display.
“The greatest among you will be your servant.”
live: Do one concrete act of justice or help for a widow, an orphan or someone who is overlooked.
Choose one thing you often tell others to do, and do it yourself today.
2027-02-23.prayer: Merciful Father, you call us to wash ourselves and learn to do good. Make our sins white as snow, free us from the love of honour, and make us servants of one another. Through the prayers of St Polycarp, faithful bishop and martyr, keep us loyal to Christ our King to the end. Amen.
altar: Christ, the one Teacher, became the servant of all and gives himself at the altar. In him our worship and our life become one offering.

quick: God invites sinners: though your sins are like scarlet, they shall be like snow.
Jesus warns against saying and not doing.
St Polycarp served Christ eighty-six years and died faithful.
2027-02-23.action: Do one hidden act of service today that no one will thank you for.
2027-02-23.question: Where does my faith stop at words and fail to become action?

family.explain: Jesus says: the greatest person is the one who serves others. People who show off will be brought low, but people who are humble will be lifted up by God.
family.intention: We pray for priests and teachers, that they may live what they teach.
family.ask: Ask: “How can each of us serve someone at home today without being asked?”

illus: An old catechism teacher in a parish near Alappuzha was known to the children for one thing: she never asked them to do anything she did not do first. When she taught them to visit the sick, she took them with her to the homes of the bedridden. Years later a former pupil, now a priest, said: I forgot most of her lessons, but I never forgot her feet walking to those houses.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, one Teacher and Master, you came to serve. Wash us and make us humble servants. Amen.
share: Cease to do evil, learn to do good (Isaiah 1:16–17). What good do I need to learn?
They do not practice what they teach (Matthew 23:3). Where do my words outrun my life?
The greatest among you will be your servant (Matthew 23:11). Whom can I serve this week?
pm.resp: To the upright I will show the saving power of God.
interc: For pastors and teachers, that they may live what they teach.
For the oppressed, orphans and widows, that justice may reach them.
For those who think their sins are too great to be forgiven.
For persecuted Christians, through the prayers of St Polycarp.
For our group, that our faith may be humble and practical.
pm.close: Father, you make scarlet sins white as snow. Teach us to serve as your Son served. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, God speaks through Isaiah to a people whose temple was busy but whose lives were not changed. Wash yourselves; make yourselves clean… cease to do evil, learn to do good; seek justice, rescue the oppressed, defend the orphan, plead for the widow (Isaiah 1:16–17).

And then the invitation: come now, let us argue it out, says the LORD: though your sins are like scarlet, they shall be like snow (Isaiah 1:18). No sin is too red for God's mercy. Lent is the time to come and reason with him in confession.

In the Gospel Jesus warns us about a faith of display: they do not practice what they teach. They love the best seats and titles. But Jesus says: the greatest among you will be your servant. All who exalt themselves will be humbled, and all who humble themselves will be exalted (Matthew 23:11–12).

Today we remember St Polycarp, bishop of Smyrna and disciple of St John. At eighty-six, when told to curse Christ, he said in substance: for eighty-six years I have served him, and he has done me no wrong; how can I blaspheme my King? He lived what he taught. May we too say and do, for Christ our King. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus says the greatest person is the one who helps others. St Polycarp was a bishop who loved Jesus all his life, even when he was very old. Let us do one kind thing today without being asked!

intro: Theme: “The greatest among you will be your servant.”
Washed from scarlet sins, freed from a religion of display, faithful like Polycarp.

q: Wash yourselves; make yourselves clean; remove the evil of your doings from before my eyes; cease to do evil, learn to do good; seek justice, rescue the oppressed, defend the orphan, plead for the widow.
Religion that is pure and undefiled before God, the Father, is this: to care for orphans and widows in their distress, and to keep oneself unstained by the world.
points.apply: Visit or help one widow, orphan or lonely person before Sunday.

points.h: Though your sins are like scarlet
q: Come now, let us argue it out, says the LORD: though your sins are like scarlet, they shall be like snow; though they are red like crimson, they shall become like wool.
If we confess our sins, he who is faithful and just will forgive us our sins and cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
points.apply: Plan your Lenten confession: choose the day and the church now.

sub: One Teacher, all brothers and sisters.
q: He has told you, O mortal, what is good; and what does the LORD require of you but to do justice, and to love kindness, and to walk humbly with your God?
The greatest among you will be your servant. All who exalt themselves will be humbled, and all who humble themselves will be exalted.
points.apply: Like Polycarp, let your life speak louder than your words: one hidden service each day this week.

concl: God washes us and asks us to do good.
Jesus makes greatness into service, and the saints show it to the end.
2027-02-23.resolve: Do one hidden act of service each day this week.
